newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer after late pick up.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer after late pick up.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer after a late run-up reversed earlier losses, placing the market onto a better technical footing to muster further gains, dealers said.
LME stocks continued with their downward trend, dipping 2,825 tonnes Wednesday to 149,300 tonnes.

Dealers said there was also talk in the market that miners at Chile's state-owned Codelco were discussing the possibility of labor action related to the reported plan to privatise Enami, a copper smelting and refining complex.
July COMEX copper settled 0.70 cent firmer at 113.80 cents per lb, traded 113.90 to 112.50 cents. Spot May went out 0.80 cent higher at 114.00 cents. Volume was estimated at 8,000 lots.

William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch said copper futures looked constructive on the technical charts, and LME three months price was poised to break through $2,440 per tonne resistance which would be a significant move on the charts.
"We have had an objective of 115.00 cents per lb for July COMEX for the last month or so, but we are going to up that to 117.00 to 118.00 cents," O'Neill said.
The LME backwardation was steady Wednesday, ending at $54/$58, barely changed from the previous session.
